title: Child-care work prevention co-occurs with higher following housing and utility hardship
source_unit: identified person with November-to-December stable SNAP pair, child-care work-prevention status, and December hardship fields

observations.period: 2024 reference year; stable no-SNAP; child care did not prevent work/more work

denominator.unit: valid person transition pairs for hardship outcomes

observations.method: Same-person November-to-December stable SNAP pair, conditioned on valid December EWORKMORE response; hardship measured in the following month with 240 Fay-BRR replicate weights.
observations.uncertainty: Annual fall child-care work-prevention status is attached to a December hardship observation; it is not a dated causal episode. Rent/mortgage and utility hardship have separate valid universes. Status flags were used for EWORKMORE and hardship fields.
observations.subgroup: Stable no-SNAP person pairs reporting no child-care work prevention.
observations.counterinterpretation: The contrast may reflect household composition, employment, care need, income, eligibility, or unmeasured resources rather than a direct effect of child-care arrangements.

related_sources.claim: The SIPP dictionary defines EWORKMORE and the hardship fields and their universes.
Prior same-person comparison establishes the care/work-prevention and time-loss measures.

boundary: This is a descriptive same-person bridge from annual fall child-care work prevention to following-month rent/mortgage and utility hardship within stable SNAP-status comparisons. It does not establish causation, benefit effects, exact event timing, care quality, household recovery, trust, or political action. Small cells and separate outcome universes remain explicit.
